audit.whatIsWrong: Both charts read Skill/Gnar/Gnar/Skill/Skill/Gnar/Gnar, handing Gnar the first-item and 2-item stages. Packet says Gnar,Gnar,Skill,Gnar,Skill,Vladimir,Vladimir, and every whys[] entry agrees with the packet.
audit.why: whys[0] says Vlad has one of the weakest level 1s and Gnar out-pokes him — that is a Gnar stage, not Skill. whys[2] says trades even out once pool is online (Skill, not Gnar). whys[3] says a banked Mega puts your hand on the lane (Gnar). whys[5] and whys[6] both say he outpaces and out-drains you — those are Vladimir stages, not Gnar.
audit.corrected: Gnar / Gnar / Skill / Gnar / Skill / Vladimir / Vladimir, proposed as one atomic group across both layers.

audit.whatIsWrong: Full-layer spike text pointed at 'Stridebreaker' with no reference to Vladimir's real timings.
audit.why: Vladimir's spikes are Sanguine Pool at 3 (28s at rank 1, falling to 16s), Hemoplague at 6 (flat 120s) and Rylai's/Liandry's at two items; Transfusion's cooldown also falls from 9s to 4.6s, which is what erases chip poke.
audit.corrected: Phase whys and the cooldown block now carry those numbers.

audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer never states what Sanguine Pool actually does (2 seconds untargetable), and never mentions anti-heal despite dosFull[2] being titled 'Build MR + anti-heal' with a boilerplate body that says nothing about healing.
audit.why: Both flagged missing interactions live here: untargetable-dodges-burst (Sanguine Pool eats a committed Wallop or GNAR!) and needs-antiheal (Transfusion and Hemoplague both heal, so Grievous Wounds timing decides extended trades). Hemoplague also amplifies all damage taken before it detonates, which is why fighting inside it is a losing trade.
audit.corrected: Stated the 2s untargetability and its 28s cooldown, Transfusion's 9s-to-4.6s decay and anti-heal timing, and Hemoplague's damage amplification.

audit.whatIsWrong: Packet defect: content late writes 'Sanguine Pools' as a verb, pluralising the ability name.
audit.why: The ability is Sanguine Pool. Verbing it reads as a wrong ability name in the audit tooling and on the page.
audit.corrected: late rewritten to use the ability name correctly, same length band.

edits.before: Boomerang + hop kite wins every melee matchup early. Identify how Vladimir contests the first waves before you commit anything.
edits.after: Vlad has one of the weakest level 1s — Mini autos plus a Boomerang out-poke Transfusion while you deny his last-hits.

edits.before: Rage management is the champion — track your own bar. Only take the trade when Vladimir's Sanguine Pool is down.
edits.after: Hyper's third-hit proc plus a Boomerang chunks him before Sanguine Pool exists at all — your cleanest window.

edits.before: Full kit online — your core pattern starts now. Keep the wave near your side so Vladimir must walk into your range.
edits.after: Pool comes online at 3 and Transfusion heals your Mini poke back, so trades even out unless Rage is banked.

edits.before: The lane-control window: trade around Sanguine Pool's cooldown and bank small leads. If ahead, freeze and deny; if behind, farm safe.
edits.after: Rage banked means a Mega Wallop stun connects — the one hard CC Sanguine Pool cannot undo once it has already landed on him.

edits.before: Mega + R against a wall is the best engage top lane owns. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Vladimir's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: You gain GNAR! at 6 but only in Mega form, so it is pure transform timing — banked Mega bullies a pre-Rylai's Vlad hard.

edits.before: Stridebreaker is your spike — force fights the moment it completes, on Sanguine Pool's cooldown.
edits.after: Transfusion sustain and his AP scaling start outpacing your form-gated Mini poke from here on.

edits.before: Two items on: your pattern is at full power. Vladimir carry threat 8.5/10 — close before the map decides instead of you.
edits.after: Rylai's and Liandry's Vlad pools through your CC and out-drains your burst — play for teamfights, never the solo 1v1.

edits.before: Bully him early — build MR, boomerang-poke, bait pool. Gnar wins the Sanguine Pool cooldown windows.
edits.after: Bully him early, rush anti-heal, bait Sanguine Pool — it is 28s at rank 1 and eats your whole commit.

edits.before: Bully him early and bait his pool. Track Sanguine Pool before every commit and keep the wave on your side.
edits.after: Bully him early and bait the pool out. Anti-heal by your first back — Transfusion heals every bit of chip back.

edits.before: Vladimir wins by landing Sanguine Pool, denying your pattern, and kiting you off the wave.
edits.after: Vladimir wins by pooling your commit, out-sustaining chip, and scaling past your form windows.

edits.before: Dodges your combo. Bait it. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: Sanguine Pool is 28s at rank 1 and 2s untargetable — bait it first.

edits.before: Vladimir wastes Sanguine Pool — commit the full pattern immediately.
edits.after: Transfusion drops to a 4.6s heal — Grievous Wounds decides long trades.

edits.before: That is Vladimir's favourite window — refuse it and half his win condition is gone.
edits.after: Two seconds untargetable eats your whole commit — hold Wallop until he surfaces.

edits.before: Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: His Transfusion drain scales with AP — MR and anti-heal beat raw HP.

edits.before: Getting caught at zero rage right after Mega ends — that 15-second window is when Gnars die.
edits.after: Free scaling buys Hemoplague (120s), which amplifies all damage on you before it detonates.

edits.before: Track Vladimir's Sanguine Pool: Dodges your combo. Bait it. When it is down — Boomerang-W + R him.
edits.after: Sanguine Pool (W, 28s) makes him untargetable 2s — it eats Wallop and GNAR!, so bait it, then commit.

edits.before: - Vladimir Sanguine Pool: matchup-defining — Dodges your combo. Bait it. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Sanguine Pool (W): 28s at rank 1, 2s untargetable — it eats Wallop and GNAR!. Bait it, then commit. - Transfusion (Q): 9s at rank 1, 4.6s at rank 5 — anti-heal it. - Hemoplague (R): 120s, amplifies all damage.

edits.before: This is where it flips and you have to be honest about it: full-AP Vlad with Rylai's and Liandry's becomes an unkillable drain threat that ignores your form-dependent burst, Sanguine Pools through your Wallop and GNAR! wall-combo, and kites your squishy Mini body. Your value pivots entirely to teamfights — your wall-ult is still one of the best engage tools in the game, so peel and engage for your carries instead of trying to 1v1 him. Close any lead before he completes two items, because the solo duel is his after that.
edits.after: This is where it flips and you have to be honest about it: full-AP Vlad with Rylai's and Liandry's becomes an unkillable drain threat that ignores your form-dependent burst, dodges your Wallop and GNAR! wall-combo with Sanguine Pool (W), and kites your squishy Mini body. Your value pivots entirely to teamfights — your wall-ult is still one of the best engage tools in the game, so peel and engage for your carries instead of trying to 1v1 him. Close any lead before he completes two items, because the solo duel is his after that.

notes: Packet defect fixed: content late verbed the ability name as 'Sanguine Pools'; rewritten to name Sanguine Pool (W) properly with the rest of the paragraph untouched. Both missing interactions (untargetable commit-dodge, anti-heal requirement) now reach the page in tldr, winCon, dosFull[0].d, dosFull[2].d and the cooldown block — dosFull[2] was titled 'Build MR + anti-heal' but its body never mentioned healing at all. Not verified: whether Sanguine Pool's untargetability removes an already-applied Wallop stun or only prevents new applications — the content layer asserts it 'can't undo it once it lands' in whys[3], spikes[1], mid and wants.you[1]; Riot's text does not state this either way, so I left those four strings alone rather than propagate or contradict them. Flagging it because it is repeated four times and is the matchup's central claim.
